ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (amended effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information by Financial Institutions and Specific Non-Financial Institutions (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Interim Measures for the Registration of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (SAMR, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or competent authority in the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at origin; then issue an Apostille certificate under the Hague Apostille Convention if the origin state is a Convention member; for a non-member state, proceed with Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in the origin state. Never chain Apostille and Consular Legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent registrar in the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at origin; then obtain an Apostille from the competent authority if the origin is an Apostille Convention state; otherwise obtain Consular Legalization from the Chinese consular post. The path is single and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing the WFOE legal representative and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign the resolution before a notary; obtain notarial certification; then apply Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable depending solely on the origin state's Convention status. No combined sequence is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company as registered with its competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a certified copy from the registrar; then notarize; then apply Apostille if the issuer is in a Convention state; otherwise apply Consular Legalization at the Chinese diplomatic mission. The two authentication methods are parallel, not sequential.

Have the letter signed and sealed by the bank officer; then notarize; then apply Apostille or Consular Legalization depending exclusively on whether the bank's state is an Apostille Convention member. Never combine both paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and beneficial controllers against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list and other OFAC sanctions programs, and the consolidated financial sanctions list issued by the People's Bank of China and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person, close family member, or known associate. Verification must include identity documents, source of wealth, source of funds, and continuous transaction monitoring. Negative news and adverse media checks must be performed against reputable commercial databases and public registries. Any positive or ambiguous match must trigger a risk assessment, escalation to the AML compliance officer, and a suspicious activity report to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center before incorporation or account opening. Sanctions screening must be repeated immediately before and after submission of incorporation documents, at account opening, and on a continuous risk-triggered basis.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_identification_requirements: The WFOE must identify each UBO individually. A UBO is any natural person who ultimately owns or controls the market entity through equity interests, voting rights, or other control rights, including through chains of ownership or control, or by other means. Where no natural person UBO is identified after exhausting all reasonable measures, the senior management personnel and the legal representative shall be recorded as the UBO in the beneficial owner information register.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_register_filing_mechanism: The WFOE must file beneficial owner information with SAMR via the enterprise registration information system within 30 days of incorporation or within 30 days after any change. Authorized government authorities may access the register lawfully under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3; the register is not open to the general public.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) / State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Registration and Name Clearance Module; local municipal SAMR online service portals for pre-registration name reservation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must consist of administrative division, chosen trade name (zihao), industry or business characteristics, and company type. For a WFOE, the Chinese name must be registered in Chinese characters; a corresponding English or pinyin transliteration is not a substitute and is typically registered as an alias only if locally permitted. If the foreign investor's name is used as the trade name, a standardized transliteration into Chinese must be approved. Pinyin romanization is accepted only as a transliteration aid; the legal name remains the Chinese-character name. Four-tier naming convention: tier 1 administrative division, tier 2 unique trade name, tier 3 industry description, tier 4 legal form 'Co., Ltd.' (有限公司).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name clearance system rejects the proposed name, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the superior SAMR within 60 days of receiving the written rejection decision, or file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court. The appeal must state the legal basis, the grounds for rejection, and the applicant's argument showing why the name complies with the Measures for the Registration and Administration of Enterprise Names and the Company Law. Before filing, the applicant may also request a new name clearance using different trade-name combinations; however, such new filing does not suspend the appeal deadline. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant must first obtain the prior ministerial-level approval or written consent of the relevant regulator. The appeal must be submitted via the same local SAMR online portal with a scanned copy of the rejection notice, the applicant's identity or qualification certification, and a power of attorney. A new name reservation may be filed in parallel while the reconsideration is pending, but the final structure should not rely on the contested name until adjudication. An administrative reconsideration decision is generally expected within 60 days, extendable by 30 days in complex cases. An administrative lawsuit must be initiated within 15 days after the reconsideration decision, or if no reconsideration is applied, within 6 months after the original rejection decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only registered address is generally impermissible for a WFOE whose business scope covers ISIC 6430 discretionary portfolio advisory and multi-family office services. Under SAMR registration rules, the registered address (住所) must be a fixed, concrete office location confirmed as lawfully usable and must match the actual place of business operations. Local tax authorities and banks treat a purely virtual mailbox as a high-risk indicator of shell or diversion activities. For a licensed asset-management-type or family-office-type business, the local financial or market regulator may require an actual office with adequate physical records custody, segregated client-asset custody arrangements, and dual-control access. A virtual address may only temporarily support a pre-license mailing or administrative contact, but it will not satisfy commercial substance requirements. Therefore, a physical office lease with a term of at least one to two years, a local business license or commercial lease registration, and a visible place of management in the same prefecture are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Probability of unannounced inspection within the first operating year is approximately 60% to 75% for a high-risk regulated financial advisory licence. Inspection checklist: (i) verify the nameplate and office lease at the registered address; (ii) inspect daily presence of the legal representative, senior managers, and compliance staff; (iii) review original incorporation documents, board resolutions, UBO register, and AML files; (iv) inspect customer due diligence files and beneficial ownership records; (v) verify segregation of client assets and custody wiring arrangements; (vi) test records of Swift or custody wire instructions; (vii) question employees regarding actual business lines; and (viii) verify that service contracts are for third-party clients and not purely intra-group. Municipal tax bureaus may also perform unannounced site visits to verify VAT invoices, payroll records, and actual business premises; failure to be physically open during business hours can trigger a tax address inquiry and suspension of invoice issuance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign parent entity certificate of incorporation notarization and authentication (Apostille or consular legalization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary and competent authority in the foreign parent's jurisdiction plus Chinese embassy/consulate if consular legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for notarial and authentication services; no official government fee for authentication in the majority of western jurisdictions; legal fee is the notary plus apostille authority tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign parent certificate of good standing issuance and notarization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign company registry; notary; apostille or consular authority as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry tariff in the origin jurisdiction plus notarial fee; if the jurisdiction imposes no official certificate fee, that portion is zero and only notary/apostille fees apply

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign parent board resolution for WFOE incorporation and legal representative appointment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary and authentication authorities in the foreign parent jurisdiction (or consular post if non-Apostille)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial drafting and certification tariff; the board resolution itself is not a government registry fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign parent articles of association certified copy and authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign registrar for certified copy; notary; apostille or consular office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry certified-copy tariff plus notary and authentication fees; if the registry provides the copy free of charge, only authentication costs apply

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter for foreign parent and authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign issuing bank; notary; apostille or consular authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank administrative fee if any, otherwise zero, plus prevailing notarization and apostille or legalization fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese WFOE company name clearance application fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) local branch via the enterprise registration online platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee charged by SAMR for name reservation; use of the free national name system

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese WFOE registration and business license issuance fee by SAMR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) local branch
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official issuance fee abolished in mainland China as of the current administrative fee reduction; no SAMR business license fee in most prefectures

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed seal engraving shop approved by public security; local public security bureau file-stamping
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for legal person seal, financial seal, tax seal, invoice seal, and contract seal set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of UBO information declaration and legal representative identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese notary public in the place of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local notary fee schedule for identity verification and certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO Register initial SAMR filing and PBOC/SAMR beneficial ownership declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and PBOC-covered reporting system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic beneficial ownership register fee is zero; if a local implementation platform imposes a nominal processing fee, it must be separately disclosed and is not included here

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial PEP and sanctions compliance screening using commercial AML database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial AML/CFT compliance database vendor and Chinese law-firm screening service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for multi-jurisdictional OFAC, UN, PBOC, and PEP screening of approximately five individuals plus two entities; per-record costs range from USD 15 to USD 60

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Engagement of local Chinese counsel for WFOE incorporation and pre-incorporation due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese law firm licensed to practice in the target jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard WFOE incorporation and Stage 1 due diligence package; otherwise subject to a law-firm engagement letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and notarized certification of Chinese translations of parent company documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public or certified translation agency in mainland China
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document translation fee based on page count plus notarized translation certification; approximate for a ten-document bundle

mandatory_licensing_and_regulatory_speci.special_license_required: Yes - if the WFOE will provide discretionary portfolio advisory or multi-family office services involving client assets, it must apply for and hold the applicable private fund manager or asset-management advisory licence from the Asset Management Association of China (AMAC), or a local financial-regulator license for private scheme advisory activities; a bare consulting company without discretionary authority does not require the asset-management license, but the ISIC 6430 scope clearly indicates a regulated activity requiring the high-risk special license.
mandatory_licensing_and_regulatory_speci.licensing_authority_and_application_path: China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) through the Asset Management Association of China (AMAC) for private securities or fund management; or the local Municipal Financial Supervision and Administration Bureau for advisory activities not falling under AMAC. Additional approval from SAMR is required for the business scope and from PBOC for asset-custody and Swift wiring settlement if client funds flow across borders.
mandatory_licensing_and_regulatory_speci.foreign_investment_access: The WFOE must be established in compliance with the Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access. The 2024 Negative List permits a pure advisory multi-family office enterprise, but if the activity constitutes a 'financial company' or falls within a restricted category, prior approval from the State Council or the relevant financial regulator is required. The final business scope in the Articles must not exceed the negative-list-allowed scope without additional approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Amendment), Articles 23-66; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020), Articles 6-12; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (2022)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Registration Bureau (or local counterpart, e.g., Shanghai Municipal Administration for Market Regulation)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for WFOE under current law; registered capital must be subscribed within the time limit specified in the Articles of Association (typically 30 years for service companies). No escrow account requirement is imposed for general consulting or advisory activities. However, if the entity engages in securities investment advisory, it must obtain a license from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) and may be subject to additional capital requirements under CSRC rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (THE 'COMPANY') ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE] AT [PLACE].

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) with limited liability on [DATE] with registration number [NUMBER];

WHEREAS, the Articles of Association of the Company provide for a board of directors consisting of [NUMBER] directors;

WHEREAS, the initial directors have been appointed by the sole shareholder, [SHAREHOLDER NAME], and have duly accepted their appointments;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board acknowledges that the registered capital of the Company is [AMOUNT] RMB, divided into [NUMBER] shares of [PAR VALUE] each. The Board confirms that the sole shareholder has subscribed to all shares in accordance with the Articles of Association. The Board authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to issue share certificates and to record the subscription in the register of members.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [BANK NAME] and [BANK NAME] for the Company. The Board designates the following individuals as authorized signatories for the operation of such accounts: [NAME], [TITLE], and [NAME], [TITLE]. Any two of the authorized signatories must jointly execute any transaction exceeding [AMOUNT] RMB. The Board further authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to execute all account opening documents and to provide specimen signatures.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [ADDRESS] as the official legal address for service of process and all statutory communications. The Board directs the Company Secretary to file the registered office notice with the State Administration for Market Regulation and to ensure that all corporate records are maintained at this address.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall have the powers and duties as set forth in the Articles of Association and as delegated by the Board. The Board authorizes the Company Secretary to prepare and file all necessary statutory documents and to act as the primary contact for regulatory authorities.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any officer or director to execute and deliver any agreements, instruments, or documents necessary to implement the foregoing resolutions and to take all such actions as may be required to give full effect to these resolutions.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in force until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

ADOPTED this [DATE] by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors.

[Signature of Director 1]
[Signature of Director 2]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) online portal (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the SAMR online system. Provide the proposed company name in Chinese (and optionally English), the intended business scope, and the shareholder details. The name must comply with the Regulations on Enterprise Name Registration and must not conflict with existing registered names or trademarks. After approval, obtain the Name Reservation Certificate, which is valid for 6 months. Ensure that the business scope description aligns with the intended multi-family office advisory services, using appropriate wording such as 'investment advisory' or 'financial consulting' to avoid regulatory ambiguity.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copy of the sole shareholder (if foreign individual) or certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent company
Proof of address of the shareholder
Proposed business scope description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict or non-compliance, modify the name and resubmit. If the rejection is based on substantive grounds, provide additional explanations or choose an alternative name. The applicant may also appeal to the SAMR within 15 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Association and Supporting Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (for foreign shareholder documents) and legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in Chinese, incorporating the registered capital, share structure, governance framework, and business scope. For foreign shareholders, notarize and legalize the certificate of incorporation, passport copies, and any power of attorney appointing a local representative. The lease agreement for the registered office must be executed and stamped. All documents must be translated into Chinese if originally in another language, with certified translations. Submit the draft Articles to the local SAMR for pre-review if required, to ensure compliance with the Company Law and Foreign Investment Law.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized shareholder documents (certificate of incorporation, passport copies)
Draft Articles of Association
Lease agreement for registered office (with property ownership certificate)
Power of attorney for local agent (if applicable)
Identity documents of the legal representative and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR queries the Articles or documents, rectify the deficiencies within 15 days. If notarization is incomplete, redo the notarization and legalization process. If the lease agreement is defective, obtain a new lease or provide additional proof of address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Registration Application to SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (e.g., Shanghai Municipal Administration for Market Regulation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete registration application online via the SAMR portal or in person at the local service window. The application package must include the signed Articles of Association, the Name Reservation Certificate, the lease agreement, shareholder identity documents, and the appointment of the legal representative. Pay any applicable registration fees (if any; typically no fee for standard registration). The SAMR will review the application and, upon approval, issue the Business License (Unified Social Credit Code). The entire process is expected to be completed within 5 working days.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of a foreign-invested enterprise
Articles of Association (signed by all shareholders)
Name Reservation Certificate
Lease agreement and property ownership certificate
Passport copies of shareholders and legal representative
Appointment documents for directors and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the SAMR's comments within 15 days. If the application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration or appeal to the higher authority within 60 days. Alternatively, correct the issues and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Procedures: Tax, Bank, Seals, and Financial Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Bureau, Public Security Bureau (for seals), Bank, and China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business License, complete tax registration with the local tax authority within 30 days, obtain a tax identification number, and register for corporate income tax and value-added tax. Apply for the company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal at the Public Security Bureau. Open a corporate bank account with the authorized bank, providing the Business License and seal. Register for social security and housing fund. If the company intends to provide discretionary portfolio advisory services, it must apply for a securities investment advisory license from the CSRC or a local financial regulatory bureau, which involves additional compliance requirements, including capital adequacy and professional qualifications.
required_dossiers: Business License (original and copy)
Tax registration form
Seal registration application
Bank account opening documents (Business License, seals, passport copies)
Social security registration form
Financial license application (if applicable) - including business plan, compliance manual, and qualification certificates of key personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, contact the tax authority to expedite. If seal registration is rejected, correct the documentation. If the financial license application is denied, the company may appeal to the CSRC or adjust its business scope to avoid regulated activities. Legal counsel should be engaged to address any regulatory hurdles.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - This entity is a financial services provider (multi-family office) and does not engage in physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activities. However, it may require a separate securities investment advisory license from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) under the Securities Law and relevant regulations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - No physical premises requiring fire safety certification or structural load inspections beyond standard office occupancy. The company must comply with general workplace safety regulations under the Work Safety Law, but no special industrial clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online portal: State Taxation Administration National Unified Standard Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax), accessible at etax.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is incorporated through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) one-stop registration window. SAMR automatically forwards the company's establishment data to the STA under the multi-certificate integration reform. The STA then issues the 18-character Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC), which legally serves as the Tax Identification Number (TIN) for all tax purposes; no separate paper tax registration certificate is issued. The legal representative or authorized financial officer must access the National Unified Electronic Tax Bureau through real-name authentication and complete the pre-starting tax registration information report within 30 days after issuance of the business license. The filing must include corporate bank account details, accounting records and bookkeeping arrangements, shareholder information, and legal representative identity. The E-Tax system automatically constructs the VAT taxpayer profile, and the taxpayer must determine whether it is a small-scale VAT taxpayer or a general VAT taxpayer. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China, the payer or withholding agent completes the Non-Resident Enterprise tax registration through the E-Tax platform, obtains a non-resident taxpayer identification code, and performs withholding registration under the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law and the Tax Collection Administration Law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The WFOE is a Chinese tax resident enterprise subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT) on its worldwide income at the standard 25% rate; no pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification purposes; the PRC does not operate a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch entity election. The only relevant election is the VAT general taxpayer registration election: an enterprise with annual taxable sales below RMB 5,000,000 may elect general VAT taxpayer status, while an enterprise exceeding that threshold must register as a general VAT taxpayer. The general VAT taxpayer status is required to claim input VAT credits and cross-border zero-rating refunds.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Law and the State Administration of Taxation implementation rules
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales (expected to be predominantly taxable services for a multi-family office advisory business); taxpayers below this threshold are small-scale VAT taxpayers with simplified taxation, while those above must register as general VAT taxpayers. Basic VAT registration is triggered by any taxable business activity with no de minimis turnover threshold for general tax liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the National Unified Standard Electronic Tax Bureau invoice platform and the VAT Invoice Management System. Fully digitalized electronic invoices (digital e-invoices) are the mandatory standard for newly registered taxpayers and are being rolled out nationwide. Invoice data is transmitted in real time to the STA through the electronic invoice service platform, and each invoice carries a unique anti-fraud encryption code, QR code, and digital tax-control stamp. VAT special invoices are reconciled against the STA invoice verification system before downstream customers may claim input VAT credits or before exporters may apply for zero-rating refunds. This is a centralized real-time invoice clearance and anti-fraud digital stamping regime rather than a distributed physical fiscal cash-register sign-off system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods may claim the 0% VAT rate only when the goods are physically declared to and leave PRC customs territory, the export sale is genuine, title and risk have passed to the overseas buyer, and the export proceeds are repatriated through authorized banking channels. For cross-border services, including discretionary portfolio advisory services supplied by a multi-family office to non-resident private clients, the services can qualify for VAT zero-rating or exemption only if the services are consumed wholly outside China, the client is a non-resident, the benefit and economic enjoyment occur outside China, the services are not resupplied into China, and the WFOE maintains contemporaneous evidence of the foreign client's identity, the cross-border contract, service delivery, invoices, and foreign exchange receipts. Advisory services that are directly connected to assets, investments, or taxable activities within China are ineligible for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration) evidencing the physical export of goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill as proof of cross-border transport of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank foreign-exchange receipt confirmation evidencing export proceeds repatriation
Cross-border service agreement or engagement letter with the non-resident multi-family office client
Detailed VAT invoice issued for the cross-border service
Overseas client tax residency certificate or legal existence evidence
Service completion and delivery documentation evidencing the provision of the advisory services outside China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may revoke zero-rating or exemption, claw back any input VAT credit or refund, and impose a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on underpaid VAT where export substantiation is missing or defective. A claim supported by false documentation is treated as fraudulent export tax refund or tax evasion under Article 63 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection, exposing the WFOE to recapture of the full tax benefit, a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax involved, and criminal liability under the PRC Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refund, which can lead to imprisonment up to life imprisonment and confiscation of property. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline without a recognized SAFE-approval extension may also trigger State Administration of Foreign Exchange penalties, loss of customs administrative facilitations, and automatic reversal of the zero-rating treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) with delegated foreign-exchange administration to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime with a clear bifurcation between current-account and capital-account convertibility. RMB is fully convertible on the current account for trade in goods and services, meaning WFOE invoice settlement, service fees, royalty and profit remittances can clear through designated banks after routine documentary review. Capital-account items remain subject to strict prior approval/registration by SAFE: FDI contributions, external loans, equity transfers and repatriation of liquidation proceeds all require a specific SAFE registration or filing, a dedicated onshore foreign-exchange capital account and an underlying transaction that passes a genuine-entity and reasonableness review. Profit remittances are allowed but are not an automatic right; they must be substantiated by an annual audit report, tax clearance certificate, board resolution and confirmation that the registered paid-in capital has been fully verified. The bank will also apply anti-round-tripping checks to ensure that the funds are not in substance moving Chinese domestic wealth offshore. In practice, convertibility is available but accompanied by heavy documentary burden, purpose-code verification, transaction-by-transaction monitoring, and strict post-verification checks by SAFE. Any attempt to use internal netting or sweeping without SAFE approval would be treated as illegal cross-border settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; a WFOE may retain 100% of goods-export FX receipts in a domestic foreign-exchange current-account or choose to settle into RMB through a designated bank. All export proceeds must be repatriated onshore within the deadline set by SAFE's trade-in-goods monitoring system (normally 90 days from the date of customs declaration; earlier or later collection must be justified). The retained funds may be used for current-account payments or settled at spot/forward rates, but any capital-account use remains restricted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions and EMI-style neobanks are not permitted to open deposit accounts, maintain FX accounts or provide payment services to a mainland-incorporated WFOE without a PBoC payment institution license. The WFOE must bank with a SAFE-designated onshore commercial bank for all capital-account flows; any fintech EMI can only operate as a white-label technology vendor reporting to a licensed domestic bank, and cannot serve as an independent clearing or settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. The statutory legal representative of the WFOE (or, in tightly limited circumstances, a senior board-authorized officer holding an original notarized power of attorney) must appear in person at the selected bank branch for facial-recognition verification and a compliance interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a high-risk multi-family-office license, and no virtual/offline fully remote account opening is permitted under current PBoC/SAFE rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The multi-family-office structure involves offshore trusts, foundation companies, or intermediate holding vehicles that obscure the identity of settlors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full ownership chart from the ultimate natural persons through every intermediary; certified copies of trust deeds, memoranda and articles of association; a UBO declaration table with passport, residential address and nationality; audited financial statements for each shareholder; and original bank reference/comfort letters from the presenting and upstream banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary investment-advisory and asset-management activity without a clear mainland financial-services license, raising the possibility of unlicensed securities advisory or collective investment scheme exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The AMAC/CSRC fund-management registration or a formal written confirmation from the regulator that the intended activity is out of scope; a legal opinion from a PRC-licensed law firm; the internal compliance and AML manual; the investment mandate template; and sample advisory agreements showing fee-only discretionary portfolio management rather than pool-based retail funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP or adverse-media flags against the principals, family members, or counterparty family offices connected to the shareholder structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean sanctions-screening reports from reputable screening databases on all directors, shareholders and UBOs; PEP declarations signed by each principal; negative-news and litigation search reports; a source-of-wealth statement backed by tax returns, sale-and-purchase contracts and prior audited financial statements; and two independent professional reference letters from know-your-customer qualified lawyers or bankers sanctioning the origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance and economic rationale red flag: The WFOE has no lease, no employees, no physical back-office and no credible local governance structure for a licensed money-management entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A long-term lease or property ownership certificate for registered office; PRC employment contracts and social-insurance contribution records for the statutory representative and compliance staff; a local board meeting calendar and minutes; recent office utility bills; and a business plan demonstrating how investment advisory decisions will be researched, executed and recorded within China.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent must first complete SAFE's Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration with the local SAFE branch or a designated bank, obtain a Foreign-Exchange Registration Code, and open a dedicated FDI capital account in a licensed domestic designated bank. Incoming injection wires must be sent via SWIFT MT103 to the beneficiary bank with China's SWIFT/CNAPS details, using SAFE's capital-account purpose code for foreign-invested enterprise equity contribution (typically 621011 for FDI settlement arising from equity investment, subject to bank-specific mapping). The remittance advice must identify the overseas payee name, the WFOE's registration code and the underlying contract. After arrival, the bank will verify the ownership/control line, screen the funds for sanction/PEP matches, and record the debit in the Foreign Exchange Capital Project Settlement and Remittance system. Settlement into RMB may occur only after each drawdown passes a genuine-transaction verification, and the company must obtain a capital verification report from a licensed PRC Chartered Public Accountant (CPA firm) before any capital increase or dividend declaration is recognized.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operational payments such as licensing fees, software subscription, management consulting, and overseas service invoices should be cleared by SWIFT MT103 through the WFOE's domestic RMB/FX current-account after submission of the invoice, contract, tax withholding voucher and SAFE current-account purpose code. For cross-border physical-trade settlements, the WFOE may issue irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) through its bank or use Documentary Collections (DP/DA), with the underlying customs declarations, transport documents and inspection certificates retained for SAFE compliance. All outbound transactions above the bank's exemption threshold are automatically reported to SAFE's cross-border receipt/payment monitoring system; any mis-declared purpose code can trigger suspension of the company's settlement privileges.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore CNY foreign-exchange forward contracts (current-account or approved capital-account exposure; NDFs are prohibited onshore and acceptable only offshore at the parent level without any onshore settlement)
FX swaps between CNY and foreign currencies for liquidity and maturity management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for hedging approved external debt under SAFE registration
Plain-vanilla CNY FX options on a real-demand hedging basis
Currency swap boundaries: only deliverable contracts with documented trade or debt exposure are allowed; speculative or uncovered instruments are prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (企业年度报告) submitted through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each calendar year, reporting on the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing results in the entity being列入经营异常名录 with publication of the irregularity; if not remedied within 3 years, the entity is moved to the serious non-compliant list (严重违法失信企业名单) and may face administrative penalty of up to RMB 10,000; in severe cases the license (营业执照) may be revoked leading to administrative strike-off and cancellation of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Return and Final Settlement (企业所得税年度汇算清缴)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax bureau directly under the jurisdiction of the WFOE's registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the calendar year following the tax year; the annual corporate income tax return and supporting schedules must be filed by that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment carries a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the overdue tax amount; late filing triggers a late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 per return (or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 depending on severity); prolonged non-payment can trigger asset freezing, legal enforcement, and ultimately compulsory deregistration with tax clearance certificate withheld.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value-Added Tax (VAT) and Additional Taxes Settlement and Report (增值税及附加税费年度结算)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the statutory monthly VAT filing deadline; annual settlement is completed through the December monthly VAT filing on or before January 15 of the following year (or as prescribed by the tax calendar for the relevant month)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; daily surcharge of 0.05% on outstanding VAT; persistent delinquency can trigger seizure of bank accounts, suspension of invoices (暂停供票), and administrative strike-off of the WFOE through compulsory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Individual Income Tax (IIT) Consolidated Return for Employees and Directors (全员全额扣缴申报年度汇总)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly payroll withholding returns due by the 15th of each following month; annual consolidated settlement for resident individual taxpayers due from March 1 to June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-withholding triggers administrative fines of 50% of the undercollected tax amount; daily surcharge of 0.05% for overdue tax; serious violations can lead to tax involution investigations and revocation of business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of the Foreign Investment Information Report (外商投资信息报告年度报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the Integrated Foreign Investment Information Management System submitted via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each calendar year, covering the prior year's ownership, control, and material transaction details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or submitting false information triggers rectification orders and administrative fines up to RMB 200,000; continued non-compliance may result in restriction of other government approvals, inability to obtain customs clearance preferences, and potential administrative revocation of legitimacy for ongoing operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statistics and Industry Surveys for Financial Services (金融业统计年度报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the local Financial Regulatory Bureau (地方金融监管局) where the multi-family office operates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year; specific date may be imposed by the licensing authority in the operating license conditions (typically March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance triggers mandatory rectification, fines up to RMB 30,000, suspension of business for statistics violations, potential revocation of the financial services license, and administrative strike-off through consequential revocation of the WFOE's business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Filing and Update of the Register of Beneficial Owners (受益所有人登记备案年度更新)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; supplementary filing to the Commercial Registration and Anti-Money Laundering authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the same January 1 to June 30 reporting window; in addition, any change in ultimate beneficial owner must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate beneficial ownership reporting incurs administrative penalties up to RMB 50,000; failure to update can trigger enhanced AML inspections, freezing of accounts by financial institutions, potential criminal liability under the Anti-Money Laundering Law, and administrative strike-off of the WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Renewal / Continuing Compliance Certificate for Multi-Family Office and Discretionary Portfolio Advisory (家族办公室业务资质年度审查)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Financial Regulatory Bureau (地方金融监督管理局) and the State Administration for Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for cross-border investment advisory activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days before the license expiry date; the original license validity period is typically one to three years, and renewal applications must be submitted at least 60 days prior to expiration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a renewed license subjects the entity to immediate cease-and-desist orders, fines ranging from RMB 100,000 to RMB 1,000,000, confiscation of unlawful gains, personal liability for senior managers, and ultimate administrative revocation of the WFOE licence followed by deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises in China are subject to statutory annual audit by a certified public accounting firm as mandated by the Company Law of the PRC. No quantitative exemption is available: every WFOE must appoint a Chinese CPA firm to audit the financial statements for the preceding fiscal year. Specific quantitative triggers further mandating an enhanced or license-specific audit apply when: (a) total assets exceed RMB 50 million (USD 7 million) on the balance sheet date; (b) annual operating revenue exceeds RMB 50 million (USD 7 million); (c) the entity acts as a multi-family office managing discretionary portfolios with aggregate assets under advisement exceeding RMB 100 million (USD 14 million); (d) the entity is classified as a financial institution or trust-like vehicle by the PBOC or local financial regulator, irrespective of size; (e) the entity has more than 25 employees at the end of the fiscal year; or (f) the entity engages in cross-border foreign exchange transactions exceeding USD 10 million per annum, which mandates a special-purpose audit report under SAFE regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the PRC (PRC GAAP) is mandatory for foreign-invested enterprises; the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) of China, which are substantially converged with IFRS, serve as the governing accounting framework. Small-scale WFOEs meeting specific size criteria may apply the simplified 'Standards for Small Business Enterprises' (小企业会计准则) but only in limited non-publicly accounted cases; however, multi-family offices typically must use full PRC GAAP due to their fiduciary and financial services nature.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Regulations on Beneficial Owner Registration issued by SAMR and PBOC, the WFOE must file initial beneficial ownership information within 30 days of incorporation. Annually, every registration change (including any transfer of shares, change in voting rights, or change in ultimate control) must be reported to the market regulator within 30 days of the change; in addition, the annual report must confirm and re-affirm the current beneficial ownership data as of December 31 of the preceding year. No 'silent' year is permitted; the annual confirmation must be made during the January 1 to June 30 annual window even if no change occurred. The register of members (股东名册) must be kept at the registered office and updated within 10 days of any transfer; failure to maintain or update the register invalidates the transfer against third parties and exposes the WFOE to penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages (担保事项登记册)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings (股东会及董事会会议记录册)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 to USD 600 per year for a registered office address service in major commercial cities (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen), including postal handling and routine authority communications
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to USD 12,000 for a typical WFOE multi-family office with moderate transaction volume, depending on size, AUM complexity, number of subsidiaries, and cross-border flows; highly complex structures may quote USD 15,000 to USD 25,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday is available to a licensed multi-family office in Mainland China. A preferential 15% Enterprise Income Tax rate may apply only to qualifying enterprises in encouraged industries located in approved preferential zones such as the Hainan Free Trade Port or selected pilot free-trade zones, provided the MFO has substantive local operations and meets the published encouraged-industry conditions. An R&D super-deduction of 100% of qualifying R&D expenses may apply to eligible technology development, but discretionary portfolio advisory and family-office administration services will rarely qualify. No patent-box or IP-box regime applies in China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A) 2017 Edition, with General Schedules and Special Schedules, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal (the national electronic tax filing system). Quarterly provisional prepayment returns are filed through the same portal using Form A interim schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation after quarterly provisional prepayment filing within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Corporate Income Tax return and final payment are due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before May 31 for a calendar-year enterprise. Quarterly provisional prepayments are due on or before April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 for the immediately preceding quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification details, taxpayer type, enterprise registration number, registered address, principal business codes (ISIC 6430 / NAICS 523920), and percentage of foreign ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, declare 100% foreign ownership. Identify the direct non-resident shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner. If treaty relief is intended on future distributions, retain the shareholder tax residency certificate, corporate book evidence, and beneficial ownership statement before filing; the return is the gateway to the annual related-party declaration schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss per the PRC GAAP income statement, including gross revenue, operating costs, administrative expenses, financial expenses, investment income, and non-operating income/expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border revenues from affiliated family trusts, portfolio-advisory fees, and custodian-related service fees must be fully recognized. Separate any China-source offshore revenue and any income arguably attributable to a non-resident principal; do not net operating costs against management fees unless contractually and commercially substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments to book profit: add-back non-deductible expenses, disallowed interest expense, excess entertainment expenses, excess advertising/promotion expenses if relevant, impairment allowances not actually incurred, and other permanent or timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review intercompany charges paid to foreign affiliates. A taxpayer that claims arm's-length management fees, risk-policy fees, or IT charges must support them with contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation, or the tax authority may add back the fees; especially scrutinize fees paid to a Hong Kong or other offshore family-office holding entity with limited personnel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation after adjustments, including deduction of carried-forward tax losses under the statutory limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a WFOE may be carried forward only 5 years. A non-resident shareholding change, name change, or restructuring does not extend the period. No loss carryback is permitted. If the enterprise has a short taxable year, the 5-year carryforward must be apportioned accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable Enterprise Income Tax rate and computed tax on taxable income. The statutory headline rate is 25%; preferential rates require separate approval or filing and competent certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Chinese-resident WFOE is taxed on worldwide income at this stage. If a non-resident enterprise is deemed to have a permanent establishment in China through the MFO activities, the non-resident is itself subject to 25% Chinese Enterprise Income Tax on China-source income attributable to that permanent establishment, and the outbound payment withholding rules may be displaced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and tax prepayments credited against the computed Enterprise Income Tax liability, including quarterly provisional CIT instalments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has overseas branches or foreign-source passive income, foreign income taxes may be creditable up to the Chinese CIT payable on that foreign income. No credit is allowed for foreign taxes paid by the non-resident parent. Quarterly prepayments by the WFOE must be reconciled; overpayments become refundable or creditable only through the final settlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, tax incentive claims, and reduced-rate calculations attached to special schedules (e.g., 15% preferential rate claim, R&D super-deduction schedule, accelerated depreciation, and qualified environmental/safety equipment credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim free-zone or preferential treatment for the MFO unless the business actually qualifies under the specific preferential catalogue and local administration has recognized substantive operations. For a high-risk discretionary portfolio advisory entity, an unsupported low-rate claim is a fatal red flag that will trigger audit and late-payment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax summary: gross dividends, interest, and royalties paid during the year to non-resident enterprises, and the resulting withholding tax liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the cross-border repatriation control line. Outbound dividends generally attract 10% statutory withholding tax; a DTA-reduced rate such as 5% may be applied only after the withholding agent holds a current tax residency certificate and a valid beneficial ownership statement. Dividend distributions to a non-resident parent from post-2007 earnings are no longer exempt from withholding; failure to report is tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure schedule, including loans, intangible property, services, cost-sharing arrangements, and management charges with associated enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A multi-family office with international family clients must simultaneously complete the Annual Related Party Transaction Report Form. If related-party tangible transactions exceed RMB 400 million, intangible or financial related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million, other related-party services exceed RMB 40 million, or group related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion, contemporaneous Local File / Master File documentation must be in place before the filing deadline. The return must be consistent with the transfer-pricing report or the filing is legally defective.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal representative declaration and signature, confirming that the return, financial statements, and supplementary schedules are true, accurate, and complete.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE, the legal representative in China must personally sign the e-filing. False certification opens the director and de facto controller to Chinese administrative exit controls and criminal prosecution for tax evasion; the corporate veil may be pierced where the company is a sham or where the directors used the WFOE to evade tax and mandatory AML/financial licensing obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is subject to Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 62: a penalty up to RMB 2,000, or up to RMB 10,000 if the failure is material. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax under Article 32. Underpayment or evasion through false filing is penalized at 50% to 500% of the tax evaded under Article 63. Once criminal thresholds are met, Criminal Law Article 201 imposes imprisonment of up to 3 years for relatively large evasion and 3 to 7 years for especially large amounts, together with a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. The responsible directors and officers who knowingly cause false filing can be prosecuted separately.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on the gross amount of dividends paid by a Chinese enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder that has no permanent establishment in China (Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 3, 27, and 37). A non-resident individual shareholder is generally subject to final withholding at 20% under the Individual Income Tax Law, subject to treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced Chinese withholding tax rate under a bilateral Double Tax Treaty, the following protocol is mandatory. First, the non-resident shareholder must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) in its jurisdiction of residence for the calendar year of the income, issued by the competent tax authority and containing the relevant tax treaty article. Second, the non-resident shareholder must completed a Beneficial Owner Statement under SAT Bulletin 2015 No. 60 demonstrating that it is the actual recipient, that it has full risk and enjoyment of the dividends, that it is not an intermediary or conduit, and that it has substantive economic presence in its residence state. Third, the documents must be delivered to the Chinese withholding agent before or at the time of distribution, and the withholding agent must report the treaty-basis withholding on the non-resident enterprise tax return. Where the DTA grants a 5% dividend rate, most Chinese treaties require the beneficial owner to have held at least 25% of the capital for a continuous 365-day period; if that test is not met, the rate is generally limited to 10%. If excess withholding was applied, the non-resident must initiate a tax agreement application under the Mutual Agreement Procedure and/or a refund claim with the State Taxation Administration; documentary evidence must be retained for at least 10 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Enterprise Income Tax withholding is 10% on royalties paid for the use of intangible property in China and on interest paid by Chinese residents to non-resident lenders without a permanent establishment; business tax value-added tax and surcharges may be additional at remittance. Treaty rates vary: dividends are frequently reduced from 10% to 5% where a 25% shareholding and beneficial ownership are proved; interest is commonly reduced to 10% or to 5% in some treaties for financial-institution lending, and royalties are commonly reduced to 10% or 7% depending on the treaty partner. The treaty-reduced rate is never automatic; the procedural documentation described above must precede the remittance or be corrected through the treaty claim/refund mechanism.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 400 million for related-party tangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for related-party intangible asset transfers and related-party financial transactions; RMB 40 million for other related-party services. Master File contemporaneous documentation is required where the multinational group's annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. These thresholds are expressed in renminbi and must be monitored using gross principal amounts for loans and gross contractual amounts for services.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime of the Gulf Cooperation Council type, but applies a substantive economic-substance doctrine under the Enterprise Income Tax Law general anti-abuse rule (Article 47), SAT Bulletin 2017 No. 6, and the beneficial-ownership tests in SAT Bulletin 2015 No. 60. A multi-family office claiming treaty benefits or intercompany fee deductions must demonstrate core income-generating activities (CIGA) in China: real offices, qualified investment staff, client-facing portfolio risk and performance committees, board decision-making records, payroll, local licenses, and custody/trade execution functions. A booking entity with no CIGA is exposed to recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, deemed withholding, and penalty-driven transfer pricing adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE files a CIT return that understates management-fee revenue, overstates intra-group service deductions, or omits cross-border dividends repatriated to the non-resident parent; the legal representative signs a false declaration while the company holds no supporting TP documentation, invoices, or board minutes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, plus a 0.05% daily late-payment surcharge. Criminal Law Article 201 criminalizes knowingly filing a false return or failing to file where taxes are evaded: the threshold is generally triggered when the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable; penalties include imprisonment up to 3 years for relatively large evasion and 3 to 7 years for extraordinarily large evasion, together with a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, supervisors, and senior managers who direct or participate in the false filing are subject to criminal prosecution as directly responsible persons. The Chinese tax authority may freeze personal bank accounts, seize properties where the corporate form is abused, and place the legal representative on an exit-control blacklist under the Tax Collection and Administration Law before the case is adjudicated. If the court pierces the corporate veil for fraudulent tax avoidance, directors and de facto controlling shareholders bear joint and several restitution liability for the tax, interest, and penalties out of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is used purely as a booking vehicle to route advisory fees, portfolio profits, or interest through Hong Kong or another low-tax jurisdiction; it has no investment staff, no local board meetings, no office, no client contracts executed in China, and no substantive risk management. The offshore shareholder nevertheless claims a reduced 5% dividend withholding rate and a DTA benefit while the Chinese WFOE deducts phantom service fees from the parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority invokes the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and SAT Bulletin 2017 No. 6, disregards arrangements lacking reasonable commercial purpose, recharacterizes the income, and denies treaty relief under the beneficial-ownership rules. The adjusted tax is collectible with interest, generally at the benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points; the associated related-party return penalties under Article 63 can add 50% to 500% of the re-determined tax. Treaty denial means the 10% statutory withholding rate applies on the total gross payment instead of the reduced treaty rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where shareholders and directors abuse the corporate legal personality to avoid withholding tax, the PRC Company Law doctrine of veil-piercing makes controlling shareholders and directors joint and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax to the extent the corporate form was used to evade statutory obligations. Directors can be made parties to tax enforcement proceedings, their personal assets can be preserved, and their exit from China can be blocked. If the scheme also produces an intentionally false tax return, Criminal Law Article 201 liability extends to the individual director who originated and implemented the paper structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Financial Activity / Money Laundering and AML Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The multi-family office accepts discretionary authority over client funds, commingles multiple family assets, gives effect to cross-border custody wires and SWIFT interbank transfers, and charges performance-based or custody fees while holding no required Chinese financial license, operating outside any approved pilot scheme, and deliberately circumventing customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, or suspicious transaction reporting for high-risk client families.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed asset-management or wealth-management activity is an illegal business operation under Criminal Law Article 225, punishable with confiscation of illegal gains, fines, and imprisonment of up to 5 years for serious conduct and more than 5 years in especially serious cases. Conduct that knowingly channels proceeds of predicate crime through the WFOE accounts constitutes money laundering under Criminal Law Article 191, carrying imprisonment of 5 to 10 years plus fines in severe cases. The anti-money laundering regulator may simultaneously impose administrative fines, suspension of activities, removal of the license, and blacklisting of the institution and its responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and de facto owners cannot escape criminal responsibility by relying on a nominee board; any director who executes or approves the payment-rail scheme can be named as a directly responsible person under Criminal Law Articles 191 and 225. Personal sanctions include asset seizure and criminal confiscation, monetary fines, imprisonment, civil restitution to defrauded family clients, travel restrictions, and prohibition from serving as a director of any licensed Chinese financial institution. The corporate veil is pierced where the managing director operates the WFOE as a mere instrumentality for the foreign principal.
